sanskrit: rākṣasaṃ mṛgarūpeṇa carantaṃ kāmarūpiṇam nihatya rāmo mārīcaṃ tūrṇaṃ pathi nyavartata
english: Having slain Mārīca — the rākṣasa who roamed in the form of a deer, a shape-shifter at will — Rāma quickly turned back upon the path.

sanskrit: tasya saṃtvaramāṇasya draṣṭukāmasya maithilīm krūrasvaro 'tha gomāyur vinanādāsya pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: As he hurried along, eager to see Maithilī, a jackal behind him cried out with a harsh, ominous shriek.

sanskrit: sa tasya svaram ājñāya dāruṇaṃ romaharṣaṇam cintayām āsa gomāyoḥ svareṇa pariśaṅkitaḥ
english: Recognising that dreadful, hair-raising cry and deeply troubled by the jackal's omen, he fell into anxious reflection.

sanskrit: aśubhaṃ bata manye 'haṃ gomāyur vāśyate yathā svasti syād api vaidehyā rākṣasair bhakṣaṇaṃ vinā
english: "Inauspicious indeed, I fear, is this howling of the jackal. May Vaidehī be safe and undevoured by the rākṣasas!"

sanskrit: mārīcena tu vijñāya svaram ālakṣya māmakam vikruṣṭaṃ mṛgarūpeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ śṛṇuyād yadi
english: "If Lakṣmaṇa were to hear that cry uttered in the form of a deer by Mārīca — who mimicked my voice as he discerned it — [he would come to me]."

sanskrit: sa saumitriḥ svaraṃ śrutvā tāṃ ca hitvātha maithilīm tayaiva prahitaḥ kṣipraṃ matsakāśam ihaiṣyati
english: "That son of Sumitrā, on hearing that voice and being urged by her — abandoning Maithilī — will quickly come here to my side."

sanskrit: rākṣasaiḥ sahitair nūnaṃ sītāyā īpsito vadhaḥ kāñcanaś ca mṛgo bhūtvā vyapanīyāśramāt tu mām
english: "Surely the rākṣasas in concert have plotted the killing of Sītā, and by taking the form of a golden deer they have lured me away from the hermitage."

sanskrit: dūraṃ nītvā tu mārīco rākṣaso 'bhūc charāhataḥ hā lakṣmaṇa hato 'smīti yad vākyaṃ vyajahāra ha
english: "Having drawn me far away, that rākṣasa Mārīca was struck by an arrow and cried out 'Ah, Lakṣmaṇa, I am slain!' — such were the words he uttered."

sanskrit: api svasti bhaved dvābhyāṃ rahitābhyāṃ mayā vane janasthānanimittaṃ hi kṛtavairo 'smi rākṣasaiḥ nimittāni ca ghorāṇi dṛśyante 'dya bahūni ca
english: "May those two, left alone by me in the forest, be safe! For it is on account of Janasthāna that I have made enemies of the rākṣasas. And today many terrible omens appear."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ cintayan rāmaḥ śrutvā gomāyuniḥsvanam ātmanaś cāpanayanaṃ mṛgarūpeṇa rakṣasā ājagāma janasthānaṃ rāghavaḥ pariśaṅkitaḥ
english: Reflecting thus, having heard the jackal's cry and realising how he had been lured away by the rākṣasa in a deer's form, the Rāghava came to Janasthāna filled with deep misgiving.

sanskrit: taṃ dīnamānasaṃ dīnam āsedur mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ savyaṃ kṛtvā mahātmānaṃ ghorāṃś ca sasṛjuḥ svarān
english: Beasts and birds approached that great soul who was wretched and downcast of mind, circling him on his left side and uttering dreadful cries.

sanskrit: tāni dṛṣṭvā nimittāni mahāghorāṇi rāghavaḥ tato lakṣaṇam āyāntaṃ dadarśa vigataprabham
english: After seeing those exceedingly dreadful omens, the Rāghava then beheld Lakṣmaṇa approaching, his lustre gone.

sanskrit: tato 'vidūre rāmeṇa samīyāya sa lakṣmaṇaḥ viṣaṇṇaḥ sa viṣaṇṇena duḥkhito duḥkhabhāginā
english: Not far off, Lakṣmaṇa — despondent — met with Rāma — despondent; the grief-stricken one met with his grief-sharing companion.

sanskrit: saṃjagarhe 'tha taṃ bhrātā jeṣṭho lakṣmaṇam āgatam vihāya sītāṃ vijane vane rākṣasasevite
english: Then the elder brother upbraided Lakṣmaṇa who had come [back], having abandoned Sītā alone in the desolate forest haunted by rākṣasas.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā ca karaṃ savyaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ raghunandanaḥ uvāca madhurodarkam idaṃ paruṣam ārtavat
english: Taking Lakṣmaṇa by the left hand, the joy of the Raghu clan spoke these harsh words — grievous yet with a gentle resonance underneath.

sanskrit: aho lakṣmaṇa garhyaṃ te kṛtaṃ yat tvaṃ vihāya tām sītām ihāgataḥ saumya kaccit svasti bhaved iti
english: "Ah, Lakṣmaṇa, what you have done is blameworthy — that you have come here abandoning Sītā, my good kinsman. May she yet be well!"

sanskrit: na me 'sti saṃśayo vīra sarvathā janakātmajā vinaṣṭā bhakṣitā vāpa rākṣasair vanacāribhiḥ
english: "I have no doubt, O hero, that the daughter of Janaka has in every way been destroyed or devoured by the forest-roaming rākṣasas."

sanskrit: aśubhāny eva bhūyiṣṭhaṃ yathā prādurbhavanti me api lakṣmaṇa sītāyāḥ sāmagryaṃ prāpnuyāvahe
english: "Yet even as these inauspicious signs multiply before me, may we still find Sītā whole, O Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: idaṃ hi rakṣomṛgasaṃnikāśaṃ pralobhya māṃ dūram anuprayātam hataṃ kathaṃ cin mahatā śrameṇa sa rākṣaso 'bhūn mriyamāṇa eva
english: "This rākṣasa who resembled a deer — having lured me and led me far away — was killed only with great effort; and even as he died, he revealed his true rākṣasa nature."

sanskrit: manaś ca me dīnam ihāprahṛṣṭaṃ cakṣuś ca savyaṃ kurute vikāram asaṃśayaṃ lakṣmaṇa nāsti sītā hṛtā mṛtā vā pathi vartate vā
english: "My mind here is wretched and joyless, and my left eye throbs with ill omen. Without doubt, Lakṣmaṇa, Sītā is no more — she has been carried off, or slain, or lies somewhere on the road."

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇaṃ dīnaṃ śūnye daśarathātmajaḥ paryapṛcchata dharmātmā vaidehīm āgataṃ vinā
english: Seeing the dejected Lakṣmaṇa returned alone, the son of Daśaratha — righteous in soul — questioned him anxiously about Vaidehī.

sanskrit: prasthitaṃ daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ yā mām anujagāma ha kva sā lakṣmaṇa vaidehī yāṃ hitvā tvam ihāgataḥ
english: "Where is that Vaidehī who followed me when I departed into the Daṇḍaka forest, O Lakṣmaṇa — she whom you have abandoned and come here?"

sanskrit: rājyabhraṣṭasya dīnasya daṇḍakān paridhāvataḥ kva sā duḥkhasahāyā me vaidehī tanumadhyamā
english: "Where is that slender-waisted Vaidehī, my companion in sorrow, as I — fallen from my kingdom and miserable — wander through the Daṇḍaka wilds?"

sanskrit: yāṃ vinā notsahe vīra muhūrtam api jīvitum kva sā prāṇasahāyā me sītā surasutopamā
english: "Without whom, O hero, I cannot endure to live even a moment — where is that Sītā, the companion of my very breath, like unto the daughter of the gods?"

sanskrit: patitvam amarāṇāṃ vā pṛthivyāś cāpi lakṣmaṇa vinā tāṃ tapanīyābhāṃ neccheyaṃ janakātmajām
english: "Sovereignty over the immortals or over the very earth itself — without that golden-hued daughter of Janaka I should not desire it, O Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: kaccij jīvati vaidehī prāṇaiḥ priyatarā mama kaccit pravrājanaṃ saumya na me mithyā bhaviṣyati
english: "Does Vaidehī still live — she who is dearer to me than life itself? Will this exile of mine, O gentle one, not prove to have been in vain?"

sanskrit: sītānimittaṃ saumitre mṛte mayi gate tvayi kaccit sakāmā sukhitā kaikeyī sā bhaviṣyati
english: "On account of Sītā, O son of Sumitrā, if both you and I perish, will that Kaikeyī then be content and happy with her desire fulfilled?"

sanskrit: saputrarājyāṃ siddhārthāṃ mṛtaputrā tapasvinī upasthāsyati kausalyā kaccin saumya na kaikayīm
english: "The wretched Kausalyā, her son dead, will attend upon Kaikeyī — Kaikeyī who has her own son and her kingdom and her purpose fulfilled. May this not be so, O gentle one."

sanskrit: yadi jīvati vaidehī gamiṣyāmy āśramaṃ punaḥ suvṛttā yadi vṛttā sā prāṇāṃs tyakṣyāmi lakṣmaṇa
english: "If Vaidehī lives, I shall return to the hermitage; if she has met her end — however blameless her conduct — I shall give up my life, O Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: yadi mām āśramagataṃ vaidehī nābhibhāṣate punaḥ prahasitā sītā vinaśiṣyāmi lakṣmaṇa
english: "If Vaidehī does not speak to me when I arrive at the hermitage — if Sītā no longer greets me with her smile — I shall perish, O Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: brūhi lakṣmaṇa vaidehī yadi jīvati vā na vā tvayi pramatte rakṣobhir bhakṣitā vā tapasvinī
english: "Tell me, Lakṣmaṇa — does Vaidehī live or not? Has that hapless woman been devoured by the rākṣasas while you were heedless?"

sanskrit: sukumārī ca bālā ca nityaṃ cāduḥkhadarśinī madviyogena vaidehī vyaktaṃ śocati durmanāḥ
english: "Tender and young, she who has never before known sorrow — Vaidehī is surely grieving now, her heart in anguish, separated from me."

sanskrit: sarvathā rakṣasā tena jihmena sudurātmanā vadatā lakṣmaṇety uccais tavāpi janitaṃ bhayam
english: "By that treacherous, utterly wicked rākṣasa — crying out 'Lakṣmaṇa!' in a loud voice — fear was surely instilled even in you."

sanskrit: śrutaś ca śaṅke vaidehyā sa svaraḥ sadṛśo mama trastayā preṣitas tvaṃ ca draṣṭuṃ māṃ śīghram āgataḥ
english: "I suspect that voice, resembling mine, was heard by Vaidehī; frightened, she sent you off, and you came quickly to find me."

sanskrit: sarvathā tu kṛtaṃ kaṣṭaṃ sītām utsṛjatā vane pratikartuṃ nṛśaṃsānāṃ rakṣasāṃ dattam antaram
english: "In every way it was a dreadful thing to abandon Sītā alone in the forest — an opportunity given to those merciless rākṣasas to act against her."

sanskrit: duḥkhitāḥ kharaghātena rākṣasāḥ piśitāśanāḥ taiḥ sītā nihatā ghorair bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Those flesh-eating rākṣasas, aggrieved by the slaughter of Khara, will surely have killed Sītā — those dreadful ones. Of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: aho 'smi vyasane magnaḥ sarvathā ripunāśana kiṃ tv idānīṃ kariṣyāmi śaṅke prāptavyam īdṛśam
english: "Alas, I am plunged into calamity in every way, O destroyer of foes! Yet what can I do now? Such, I believe, was the fate destined to befall."

sanskrit: iti sītāṃ varārohāṃ cintayann eva rāghavaḥ ājagāma janasthānaṃ tvarayā sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Thus brooding on Sītā of noble bearing, the Rāghava arrived hastily at Janasthāna together with Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: vigarhamāṇo 'nujam ārtarūpaṃ kṣudhā śramāc caiva pipāsayā ca viniḥśvasañ śuṣkamukho viṣaṇṇaḥ pratiśrayaṃ prāpya samīkṣya śūnyam
english: Reproaching his younger brother who looked stricken with grief, heaving sighs, his mouth parched with hunger, exhaustion and thirst, despondent — upon reaching the dwelling and seeing it empty,

sanskrit: svam āśramaṃ saṃpravigāhya vīro vihāradeśān anusṛtya kāṃś cit etat tad ity eva nivāsabhūmau prahṛṣṭaromā vyathito babhūva
english: — the hero entered his hermitage, searched through the various places she had frequented, murmuring 'here — there,' and throughout the dwelling place his body-hair stood erect in anguish.

sanskrit: athāśramād upāvṛttam antarā raghunandanaḥ paripapraccha saumitriṃ rāmo duḥkhārditaḥ punaḥ
english: Then, as he turned back from the hermitage on the way, the joy of the Raghu clan — Rāma, tormented by grief — questioned the son of Sumitrā once more.

sanskrit: tam uvāca kimarthaṃ tvam āgato 'pāsya maithilīm yadā sā tava viśvāsād vane viharitā mayā
english: He said to him: "Why have you come back having abandoned Maithilī, when she was wandering in the forest entrusted by me to your care?"

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaivābhyāgataṃ tvāṃ me maithilīṃ tyajya lakṣmaṇa śaṅkamānaṃ mahat pāpaṃ yat satyaṃ vyathitaṃ manaḥ
english: "On seeing you come back having left Maithilī, O Lakṣmaṇa, I suspect some great evil has occurred — truly my heart is anguished."

sanskrit: sphurate nayanaṃ savyaṃ bāhuś ca hṛdayaṃ ca me dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇa dūre tvāṃ sītāvirahitaṃ pathi
english: "My left eye throbs, and so does my arm and my heart, O Lakṣmaṇa, seeing you from afar on the road, separated from Sītā."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu saumitrir lakṣmaṇaḥ śubhalakṣaṇaḥ bhūyo duḥkhasamāviṣṭo duḥkhitaṃ rāmam abravīt
english: Thus addressed, the son of Sumitrā — Lakṣmaṇa of auspicious marks — himself overwhelmed with grief, spoke to the grieving Rāma.

sanskrit: na svayaṃ kāmakāreṇa tāṃ tyaktvāham ihāgataḥ pracoditas tayaivograis tvatsakāśam ihāgataḥ
english: "I did not come here of my own accord, wilfully abandoning her; I was urged by her herself with harsh and vehement words to come to your side."

sanskrit: āryeṇeva parikruṣṭaṃ hā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca paritrāhīti yad vākyaṃ maithilyās tac chrutiṃ gatam
english: "Maithilī heard those words — as if your noble cry: 'Ah, Sītā! Lakṣmaṇa! Save me!' — and it entered her ears."

sanskrit: sā tam ārtasvaraṃ śrutvā tava snehena maithilī gaccha gaccheti mām āha rudantī bhayavihvalā
english: "She, Maithilī, hearing that voice of distress and moved by her love for you, said to me 'Go, go!' — weeping, overcome with fear."

sanskrit: pracodyamānena mayā gaccheti bahuśas tayā pratyuktā maithilī vākyaṃ idaṃ tvatpratyayānvitam
english: "As I repeatedly urged 'Go!' upon her, Maithilī answered back to me with these words directed at you in full confidence:"

sanskrit: na tat paśyāmy ahaṃ rakṣo yad asya bhayam āvahet nirvṛtā bhava nāsty etat kenāpy evam udāhṛtam
english: "'I see no rākṣasa that could bring danger to him. Be calm; this is nothing — it has been spoken so by no one of consequence.'"

sanskrit: vigarhitaṃ ca nīcaṃ ca katham āryo 'bhidhāsyati trāhīti vacanaṃ sīte yas trāyet tridaśān api
english: "'How could that noble one — who could protect even the thirty gods — utter words of supplication, "Save me!"? Such words are base and unworthy of him, O Sītā.'"

sanskrit: kiṃnimittaṃ tu kenāpi bhrātur ālambya me svaram visvaraṃ vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ lakṣmaṇa trāhi mām iti na bhavatyā vyathā kāryā kunārījanasevitā
english: "'For what reason has someone, borrowing my brother's voice, cried out discordantly: "Lakṣmaṇa, save me"? You need not be distressed by this — it is the way of foolish, base women.'"

sanskrit: alaṃ vaiklavyam ālambya svasthā bhava nirutsukā na cāsti triṣu lokeṣu pumān yo rāghavaṃ raṇe jāto vā jāyamāno vā saṃyuge yaḥ parājayet
english: "'Enough of this faintheartedness — be composed, free of anxiety. There is no man in the three worlds, born or yet to be born, who could defeat the Rāghava in battle.'"

sanskrit: evam uktā tu vaidehī parimohitacetanā uvācāśrūṇi muñcantī dāruṇaṃ mām idaṃ vacaḥ
english: "Thus addressed, Vaidehī — her mind utterly bewildered — wept and then spoke these harsh words to me:"

sanskrit: bhāvo mayi tavātyarthaṃ pāpa eva niveśitaḥ vinaṣṭe bhrātari prāpte na ca tvaṃ mām avāpsyasi
english: "'Your feelings toward me are utterly base and sinful! With your elder brother dead or in peril, you think you will obtain me — but you shall not!'"

sanskrit: saṃketād bharatena tvaṃ rāmaṃ samanugacchasi krośantaṃ hi yathātyarthaṃ nainam abhyavapadyase
english: "'By prior arrangement with Bharata you accompany Rāma — yet although he now cries out in great anguish, you do not go to him!'"

sanskrit: ripuḥ pracchannacārī tvaṃ madartham anugacchasi rāghavasyāntaraprepsus tathainaṃ nābhipadyase
english: "'You are a secret enemy moving covertly, following along for my sake, seeking an opportunity against the Rāghava — that is why you do not go to him!'"

sanskrit: evam ukto hi vaidehyā saṃrabdho raktalocanaḥ krodhāt prasphuramāṇauṣṭha āśramād abhinirgataḥ
english: "Thus spoken to by Vaidehī, I became enraged, my eyes reddened, my lips quivering with fury, and I departed from the hermitage."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ saumitriṃ rāmaḥ saṃtāpamohitaḥ abravīd duṣkṛtaṃ saumya tāṃ vinā yat tvam āgataḥ
english: To Lakṣmaṇa speaking thus, Rāma — deluded by anguish — said: "You have done ill, gentle one, in coming here without her."

sanskrit: jānann api samarthaṃ māṃ rakṣasāṃ vinivāraṇe anena krodhavākyena maithilyā niḥsṛto bhavān
english: "Though knowing full well that I am capable of repelling rākṣasas, you departed at the angry word of Maithilī."

sanskrit: na hi te parituṣyāmi tyaktvā yad yāsi maithilīm kruddhāyāḥ paruṣaṃ śrutvā striyā yat tvam ihāgataḥ
english: "I am not at all pleased with you for abandoning Maithilī and coming here, having heeded the harsh words of an angry woman."

sanskrit: sarvathā tv apanītaṃ te sītayā yat pracoditaḥ krodhasya vaśam āgamya nākaroḥ śāsanaṃ mama
english: "In every way it was an unwise act on your part: urged on by Sītā, you fell under the sway of anger and did not observe my command."

sanskrit: asau hi rākṣasaḥ śete śareṇābhihato mayā mṛgarūpeṇa yenāham āśramād apavāditaḥ
english: "That rākṣasa who lured me away from the hermitage in the form of a deer — he now lies slain, struck down by my arrow."

sanskrit: vikṛṣya cāpaṃ paridhāya sāyakaṃ salīla bāṇena ca tāḍito mayā mārgīṃ tanuṃ tyajya ca viklavasvaro babhūva keyūradharaḥ sa rākṣasaḥ
english: "Drawing the bow and fitting the arrow, with ease I struck him; and that rākṣasa — he who wore bracelets on his upper arms — abandoned his deer-form and cried out in a distorted voice."

sanskrit: śarāhatenaiva tadārtayā girā svaraṃ mamālambya sudūrasaṃśravam udāhṛtaṃ tad vacanaṃ sudāruṇaṃ tvam āgato yena vihāya maithilīm
english: "Even as he was struck by the arrow, in his agonised voice he mimicked my voice and cried out from afar that dreadfully cruel utterance — it is on account of that cry that you came here, abandoning Maithilī."
